title: Process to result
premise: Something made, start to finish — a meal, a setup, a repair. Chronological and endlessly repeatable. This is where cooking lives.

copy.hook: 40 grams of protein in four minutes

shots.what: The finished result, shown first — the plate, the finished setup
shots.subject: none
shots.shoot: Shoot the end first and open with it. Nobody watches a process for a result they have not been shown.

shots.what: Everything laid out before you start — ingredients, tools, parts
shots.subject: none
shots.shoot: Straight down from above, everything in one frame, evenly lit. This is the shot that earns the save.

shots.what: First action — the cut, the crack, the pour
shots.subject: optional
shots.shoot: Close, at counter height, hands entering from the side. Keep your body out of the light.

shots.what: Second action — the one with heat, steam, or visible change
shots.subject: optional
shots.shoot: The shot with movement in it — bubbling, sizzling, steam. Backlight it if you can; steam is invisible front-lit.

shots.what: Third action — the assembly, the fold, the fit
shots.subject: optional
shots.shoot: Slow your hands down about a third. Real speed reads as fumbling on camera.

shots.what: The result completed — the cut into it, the first bite, the thing working
shots.subject: optional
shots.shoot: 4K60 if anything moves — a yolk breaking, cheese pulling, sauce running. The one moment worth slowing down.

shots.what: You, in frame with it — eating, using it, done
shots.subject: required
shots.shoot: Set the camera down and step in. A process reel with no person is a stock video.

shots.what: The finished result again, matching the opening frame
shots.subject: none
shots.shoot: Identical framing to shot 1 so the loop closes. Keep the middle clear for the text.
